reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Initial license application, fees, and attestation
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: completed application on board form, application fee payable to DHSS, and signed attestation of truth and correctness.

headings.title: Initial license qualifications, experience, and examinations
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2(1)-(3): high school diploma/equivalent, qualifying health-care administration experience/education/training, board exams, third-failure course requirement, non-recognition of out-of-state national scores after third failure, and § 536.021 cost-recovery exam fees.

headings.title: Christian Science nursing home administrator exemption and endorsement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: exempts administrators of Commission-certified Christian Science institutions from non-conforming technical/educational requirements, with license endorsed to confine practice to such institutions.

headings.title: Permissive temporary emergency license and limits
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to reflect permissive 'may issue'. Verified sub 4 and footnote (*'and' in original rolls for 'one hundred * twenty days'): up to 120-day acting administrator license replacing a deceased/removed/vacated administrator; barred for persons with prior denial, suspension, or revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.030 (bid 48852), all four subsections with subdivisions (1)-(3), history (L. 1969 through A.L. 2020 merged bills), and original-rolls footnote (*Word 'and' appears in original rolls for 'one hundred * twenty days'). Tightened sub 4 title to reflect permissive 'may issue' temporary emergency license authority.

headings.title: License expiration, renewal filing, and fee
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to include May renewal filing, CE evidence, and DHSS fee. Verified sub 1: June 30 biennial expiration with 2006 1- or 2-year transition proviso.

headings.title: Incomplete renewal application and temporary permit
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: mandatory 30-day temporary permit on incomplete renewal application (extensible 30 days for good cause); board 'may refuse' renewal if documentation/fee not timely submitted.

headings.title: Mandatory license renewal upon meeting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: board shall renew the license of an applicant who meets all renewal requirements.

headings.title: Optional continuing education cap and provider fee
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to reflect permissive 'may require' cap of 48 clock hours/year. Verified sub 4: board-approved CE and separate nonrefundable single-offering provider fee under § 536.021.

headings.title: Board renewal notification, applicant submission, and attestation
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: board must notify renewing licensees by April 1; applicant must submit renewal information attested by signature.

headings.title: Late relicensure, penalty, and twelve-month expiration rule
headings.reviewNote: Corrected draft note and refined title. Verified sub 6: post-June 30 relicensure requires renewal fee plus $25 penalty; no additional action for <=2-month expiration if clean 5-year record and other requirements met (except § 344.050 discipline); >12-month expiration requires initial licensure under § 344.030.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.040 (bid 18374), all six subsections, and history notes (L. 1969 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 80). Corrected drafter-2 hallucination in sub 6 note (actual penalty is $25, not 10%/month, with a 2-month safe harbor and 12-month initial-licensure reset) and refined titles for subs 1, 4, and 6.

headings.title: Complaint intake procedures, logging, and status notification
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: board receives complaints, adopts pre-AHC handling rules with logging requirements, and informs complaining parties of progress, dismissal, or AHC filing.

headings.title: Pre-review confidentiality of complaints and investigatory records
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: notwithstanding any other law, no complaint, investigatory report, or information received from any source may be disclosed before board review.

headings.title: Discretionary disclosure to licensees for investigations or settlement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: board 'may' disclose complaints, completed investigatory reports, and state agency/law-enforcement info to a licensee or applicant to further investigation or settlement.

headings.title: Consent prerequisite for federal agency information disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: information from a federal administrative or law enforcement agency may be disclosed only upon written consent of that federal agency.

headings.title: Discretionary disclosure for interstate exchange and agency requests
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5(1)-(3): board 'may' disclose complaints and investigatory reports for voluntary interstate exchange, lawful requests, or authorized state/federal agencies.

headings.title: Confidentiality of closed proceedings and public final decisions
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 6: except as authorized in § 344.045 and § 610.021, deliberations, votes, and minutes of closed proceedings are not subject to disclosure or discovery; final dispositions are made available to parties and the public.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.045 (bid 54252), all six subsections with subdivisions (1)-(3), and source note (L. 2023 S.B. 157). Verified complaint logging/notification duties, pre-review confidentiality, discretionary disclosures, federal written-consent requirement, and closed-proceeding protection.

headings.title: Refusal to issue or renew, probationary license, and hearing rights
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: board 'may refuse' issuance/renewal or 'may, at its discretion,' issue a probationary license for sub 2 causes; requires written notice and 30-day AHC review request window (waived if untimely).

headings.title: Grounds for disciplinary complaint before administrative hearing commission
headings.reviewNote: Corrected note count to 16 causes (not 18). Verified sub 2(1)-(16): board 'may' file a chapter 621 AHC complaint against holders or lapsed/surrendered holders, including § 324.012 offenses and chapter 198 facility/reporting grounds.

headings.title: No interim AHC authority to compel initial licensure
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 3: the AHC has no authority to require issuance of a license pending a final determination in any initial-licensure case.

headings.title: Notice and hearing required before adverse action
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 4: no license may be suspended or revoked and no renewal application denied under § 344.050 without opportunity for hearing after due notice under §§ 621.015–621.205.

headings.title: Permissive board discipline and five-year reapplication bar
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 5: upon AHC finding of sub 2 grounds, board 'may' censure, place on probation, suspend, or revoke, and 'may' exclude reapplication for up to five years after revocation or surrender.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.050 (bid 48462), all five subsections including all 16 subdivisions of sub 2, and history notes (L. 1969 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Replaced hallucinated draft titles and notes for subs 3, 4, and 5 (and corrected sub 2 subdivision count from 18 to 16) to match the archived text.

headings.title: Confidentiality of applicant and licensee records; board privileges
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 1: transcripts, test scores, complaints, investigatory reports, and applicant/licensee info are confidential except with written consent (in which case board shall disclose); board holds attorney-client and work-product privileges.

headings.title: Discretionary disclosure without consent for agencies and requests
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 2(1)-(3): notwithstanding sub 1, board 'may' disclose confidential info without consent for voluntary interstate exchange, lawful requests, or authorized administrative/law-enforcement agencies.

headings.title: Nonconfidential licensee and applicant identity information
headings.reviewNote: Replaced mismatched draft title/note. Verified sub 3: names, addresses, registration, and license currency of licensees, and names and addresses of applicants, are not confidential information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.055 (bid 54253), all three subsections with subdivisions (1)-(3), and source note (L. 2023 S.B. 157). Replaced all three hallucinated draft titles and notes to match the actual archived provisions on applicant/licensee record confidentiality, consent exceptions, and nonconfidential identity data.

headings.title: Board creation and member composition
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: governor appoints 10 members with senate consent, who with the DHSS director/designee form the Missouri Board of Nursing Home Administrators within DHSS.

headings.title: Member qualifications, residency, and conflict of interest limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: sets professional breakdown (1 physician, 2 health professionals, 1 health-care educator, 4 administrators with 5-year experience, 2 public members), citizenship/residency/voter rules, and financial-interest bars.

headings.title: Member terms, staggered expiration, and vacancy appointments
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: 3-year terms with at most 4 expiring per year, vacancy appointments by governor, and holdover service not extending the 3-year term.

headings.title: Certificate of appointment and oath of office
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: each member receives a certificate of appointment and must take the Article VII, Section 11 constitutional oath before entering duties.

headings.title: Governor removal of board members for cause after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: governor 'may' remove any member for misconduct, incompetency, or neglect of duty after opportunity to be heard.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.060 (bid 18376), all five subsections, and history notes (L. 1969 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Verified 11-member board composition, detailed qualification/conflict bars, 3-year staggered terms, constitutional oath, and permissive gubernatorial removal for cause. Retained all five titles.

headings.title: Board officers, seal, recordkeeping, and operational expenses
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: annual election of president/VP/secretary, seal, application/complaint preservation, register, evidentiary status of certified copies, and permissive hiring/expenses within appropriations.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority, administrative rules review, and suspension procedure
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: rulemaking under chapter 536 for §§ 344.020–344.108, committee on administrative rules AHC challenge with immediate suspension and 10-day hearing, and § 536.024 prerequisite.

headings.title: Licensure duties, disciplinary hearings, and prosecutor referrals
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: examine/license/renew qualified applicants, hold due-process disciplinary hearings, and refer §§ 344.010–344.108 violations to prosecuting attorneys.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.070 (bid 18377), all three subsections, and history notes (L. 1969 through A.L. 2007 merged bills). Verified annual officers, certified-record evidentiary status, permissive staffing, chapter 536/AHC rule challenge suspension, and licensure/prosecutor referral duties. Retained all three titles.

headings.title: Eligibility and affidavit procedure for license retirement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: administrators with 10+ years active licensure may retire via verified affidavit or signed renewal-application request before June 30, with fee payable to DHSS.

headings.title: Surrender of license credentials upon retirement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: applicant must return original wall license and indicia (or prove loss/theft/destruction), after which board issues a new license indicating retired status.

headings.title: Reactivation requirements within five years and continuing education
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: reactivation within 5 years requires 20 clock hours CE per retired calendar year (completed beforehand) plus fee; after 5 years, initial licensure under § 344.030 applies.

headings.title: Prohibition on practice and holding out under retired license
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: prohibits practicing or holding oneself out as a nursing home administrator in Missouri while license is retired.

headings.title: Ongoing disciplinary jurisdiction over retired licensees
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: retired licensees remain subject to disciplinary action for violations of chapter 344 and its rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.105 (bid 18380), all five subsections, and history notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1591 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Verified 10-year active-license retirement eligibility, credential surrender and retired-license issuance, 5-year reactivation with 20 CE hours/year, practice bar, and ongoing discipline. Retained all five titles.

headings.title: Inactive license status application, continuing education, and fee
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: current licensee may request inactive status via signed request or renewal form before June 30, with 10 clock hours patient-care CE and DHSS fee.

headings.title: Surrender of licensure indicia for inactive status
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: applicant must return all licensure indicia or submit satisfactory evidence of loss, theft, or destruction.

headings.title: Inactive license expiration and biennial renewal procedure
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: expires June 30 of second year after issuance and biennially thereafter; May renewal requires 10 clock hours patient-care CE and fee.

headings.title: Maximum six-year inactive status duration and expiration
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: inactive status may be carried up to 6 years from issuance, expiring on the last day of the 6-year period if not reactivated.

headings.title: Reactivation application, continuing education, and interim license
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: reactivation requires written request, fee, and completion/plan for 40 CE hours (earned within 6 months before to 12 months after); board issues 6-month interim license if hours pending.

headings.title: Sworn statement of non-practice for reactivation
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 6: reactivation request must include sworn/affirmed statement of non-practice during inactive period and presently in Missouri.

headings.title: Prohibition on practice and holding out while license is inactive
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 7: prohibits practicing or holding oneself out as a nursing home administrator while license is inactive.

headings.title: Disciplinary jurisdiction over inactive licensees
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 8: inactive licensees remain subject to discipline for violations of chapter 344 and rules promulgated thereunder.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 344.108 (bid 18381), all eight subsections, and history notes (L. 2007 H.B. 780, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Verified inactive-status application, indicia surrender, biennial renewal, 6-year cap, 40-hour CE reactivation and 6-month interim license, sworn non-practice statement, practice bar, and ongoing discipline. Retained all eight titles.
